items.body_excerpt:
NRL Casualty Ward: Reynolds struck down; Double blow for Sharks
The Broncos were dealt a blow early in their clash with the Knights with Adam Reynolds leaving the field after a head knock.
The halfback tried to tackle Greg Marzhew front-on in the seventh minute of the clash at Suncorp Stadium but his head copped the winger's shoulder and he was deemed a Category 1 head knock and ruled out for the night.
Forward Xavier Willison left the field around the same time as Reynolds with a nasty gash to his leg. The Broncos initially hoped Willison would return but he did not get back on the field.
There was also drama in the warm-up for Brisbane with Payne Haas injuring his shoulder, however the prop received treatment and was able to take his place in the starting side.
The Broncos went into the match without Preston Riki , who has had surgery to repair a syndesmosis injury suffered in Round 21 against the Cowboys.
In Sunday's opening game, the Sharks lost both centre KL Iro and utility Sifa Talakai in their game against the Bunnies.
Iro failed his HIA in the first half, while Talakai came off with a biceps injury.
Following the match, coach Craig Fitzgibbon was hopeful Talakai's injury wasn't as bad as first feared.
"It's the top end, so it's not the bottom end, the bottom end means you're out, you're gone, it's the top end, so it's not as bad ... he's definitely done something to it, so we've got to work out what the time frame on that is, which was disappointing for us ..."
In Saturday's first game of the day, Titans halfback Zane Harrison came from the field late in the second half with a suspected hamstring injury.
Harrison had to be helped from the field by a trainer in the 75th minute as the Titans fell to a 42-6 loss.
"It's too early to tell," Titans coach Josh Hannay said when asked about the severity of the injury. "When I first saw it, the nature of it being his own doing, I was worried it was his knee.

"It's his hamstring, we know that for sure so that's a slight positive because it could've been much worse."
The Warriors lost Demitric Vaimauga following captain's run with a ribs complaint, but he is only expected to miss one week.
The Dragons lost hard-working forward Toby Couchman to a failed HIA at WIN Stadium on Friday night.
Storm playmaker Jahrome Hughes was a late withdrawal from Friday night's clash against the Bulldogs due to hamstring tightness.
Centre Jack Howarth missed the match after injuring his shoulder at training while Harry Grant (hamstring) and Cameron Munster (knee) are also sidelined.
The Raiders suffered a blow ahead of their trip to Mudgee with gun centre Simi Sasagi ruled out with a hamstring injury.
Sasagi joined forward Noah Martin (quad) in the Raiders' casualty ward.
In Round 23's opening match, Roosters captain James Tedesco didn't play in the second half of his side's record 82-12 win over the Cowboys, sitting out the second half with ice on his left ankle.
However, the club weren't too concerned, with coach Trent Robinson saying Tedesco had informed him he was 'right to go' - but given the score, they opted to sit him out.
"There was a choice around his ankle, he was going okay, so I think he did it in the first five minutes," Robinson told reporters post-game.
"I saw him hobbling and ... he had a pretty good first half, and he said he was right to go, and I as a coach is sort of there going, 'I really want to set the tone again for the start of the second half', so you want to send your captain out there and the scoreline was what it was anyway, I decided to put Cody out there.
"Teddy said he's right to go if needed ... so it was just a decision and Cody did a pretty good job in the second half for us."
The Roosters were without veteran winger Daniel Tupou who is out for the next month after he dislocated his shoulder in Rou

NRL 2026 team lists: Every club's predicted lineup for Round 23
Peter Maniaty
Getty Images
Round 23 begins with a Queensland derby on Thursday night as the Titans and Cowboys lock horns on the Gold Coast.
Friday sees two potential finals previews as the Warriors host Penrith in Auckland and the Roosters meet the Bulldogs at Allianz in Sydney.
The Storm and Sea Eagles clash at HBF Stadium in Perth on Saturday afternoon in the city's final NRL match before the arrival of its own team next March, followed by the latest instalment of the 'Battle of Brisbane' at Suncorp.
The Dragons and Sharks close out the round on Sunday afternoon at Kogarah.
The Tigers have the bye this week.

Titans team news:
Zane Harrison left the field in the loss to the Warriors with a hamstring injury and looks set for some time on the sidelines, with Lachlan Ilias likely to come into the halves.
North Queensland predicted team:

John Bateman (hamstring) was a late withdrawal in Round 22 and will try again this week. Tom Dearden (ankle) remains out, but Reed Mahoney should return at No. 9.

Sharks’ late switch as gun benched; Bunnies’ huge call on emerging star — Late Mail
Souths have elected to err on the side of caution with the versatile Tallis Duncan, who is battling a hamstring injury.
Watch every game of every round of the NRL Premiership LIVE with no ad-breaks during play on FOX LEAGUE, available on Kayo Sports | New to Kayo? Join now and get your first month for just $1 .
Meanwhile, the Sharks have made a surprising call on one of their best players.
Read on for Round 22 Late Mail!
SUNDAY AUGUST 2
Cronulla Sharks vs South Sydney Rabbitohs, 2pm @ Ocean Protect Stadium
Sharks Team: 1. William Kennedy 2. Sione Katoa 3. Jesse Ramien 4. KL Iro 5. Ronaldo Mulitalo 6. Braydon Trindall 7. Nicho Hynes 16. Oregon Kaufusi 9. Blayke Brailey 17. Jesse Colquhoun 11. Briton Nikora 12. Teig Wilton 13. Cameron McInnes 8. Addin Fonua-Blake 10. Thomas Hazelton 14. Siosifa Talakai 15. Billy Burns 19. Jayden Berrell 21. Samuel Stonestreet
Players cut: 18. Mawene Hiroti 20. Braden Hamlin-Uele 22. Niwhai Puru
Late Mail: Addin Fonua-Blake and Tom Hazelton have been dropped to the bench to start the game, replaced by Jesse Colquhoun and Oregon Kaufusi.
Rabbitohs Team: 1. Matthew Dufty 2. Alex Johnston 3. Latrell Siegwalt 4. Jack Wighton 5. Campbell Graham 6. Cody Walker 7. Ashton Ward 8. Tevita Tatola 9. Brandon Smith 10. John Radel 11. Keaon Koloamatangi 22. Adam Elliott 13. Lachlan Hubner 14. Jye Gray 15. Jamie Humphreys 16. Liam Le Blanc 17. Sean Keppie 18. Jayden Sullivan 20. Thomas Fletcher
Players cut: 19. Edward Kosi 21. Tallis Duncan 12. Euan Aitken
Late Mail: Tallis Duncan was always up against it to play, being named on the extended bench and it’s now being revealed the versatile star won’t line up for the Bunnies. According to Code Sports , the Rabbitohs will err on the side of caution with Duncan’s hamstring injury. He is set to return next week along with Cameron Murray according to coach Wayne Bennett. There is less certainty around Latrell Mitchell , with Bennett telling reporters the “timeline (for him to return) is when he’s fit”. Elsewhere, Bennett said Dayne Jennings is not running yet but that “we won’t see much of him before the season is over” after he badly cut his leg against Penrith. “He got an infection in it so he spot seven or eight days in hospital,” Bennett added. Euan Aitken has been dropped with Adam Elliott to take his place in the starting side.

Late Mail: Coach Benji Marshall told reporters on Wednesday the decision to recall Adam Doueihi to the halfback jumper was simply based on what he thought was best for the team’s chances of winning. “Sometimes you’ve got to put your ego to the side and think about what the team actually needs and what the club needs and what we’re going through and what our fans need is a win,” Marshall said.

Players cut: 21. Ryley Smith 22. Jonah Pezet 20. Araz Nanva
Late Mail: Front rower Luca Moretti will miss Sunday’s game with a concussion but is expected to return for Round 23 along with Sean Russell (adductor) and Bailey Simonsson (ankle) according to Parramatta’s latest injury update.
